findings.message: Two distinct C2 violations co-located in BDD.01.03.9b90, requiring co-resolution. (1) Compound When block: 'When the Shorten/Redirect API acknowledges the issued short code' is one When-phase trigger; 'And the Mapping Store is hard-killed before any post-acknowledgement flush' is a second distinct system-level trigger appended via 'And'. Two independent triggers on different system components violate one-action-per-When atomicity and make it impossible to isolate a failure to either path. (2) Missing numeric timeout on the async Then: 'after the Mapping Store restarts the issued short code SHALL still resolve to the original URL' is an in-scenario async wait with no declared numeric timeout or polling ceiling, leaving step-definition authors unable to bound how long to wait before failing the assertion, making the step environment-sensitive.
findings.recommendation: Restructure the scenario to address both gaps in one edit pass. Move the API acknowledgement and hard-kill to Given preconditions (treating them as established context), leaving exactly one explicit When trigger (the restart). Add a named threshold key to the restart-and-resolve wait: bind the post-restart resolution time under the RTO key implied by EARS.01.04.5e5b (RTO <= 30 min) or carry @threshold:PRD.01.perf.redirectp95 on the resolve assertion. Resulting shape: Given the Shorten/Redirect API has acknowledged the issued short code / And the Mapping Store has been hard-killed before any post-acknowledgement flush / When the Mapping Store restarts / Then the issued short code SHALL still resolve to the original URL within @threshold:<rto-key>.

findings.message: Compound And-step bundles two independently falsifiable assertions in one step line: 'the 1,000 issued codes SHALL be pairwise distinct AND SHALL pass a monobit frequency test over their concatenated bit-string at the significance level @threshold:PRD.01.security.codeentropy'. Pairwise distinctness (a uniqueness / collision property) and monobit frequency (a statistical entropy property) are separate, independently testable observables. A collision failure cannot be distinguished from an entropy-distribution failure when both are asserted in the same step. The 'AND' conjunction within a single step line is a direct C2 violation.
findings.recommendation: Split the compound And-step into two separate step lines: 'And the 1,000 issued codes SHALL be pairwise distinct' (uniqueness assertion) followed by 'And the 1,000 issued codes SHALL pass a monobit frequency test over their concatenated bit-string at the significance level @threshold:PRD.01.security.codeentropy' (entropy assertion). Each step then maps to one independently reportable test assertion.

findings.message: Dual-plane outcome co-location impairs failure attribution. The Then block asserts three outcomes spanning two distinct observability planes: (1) behavioral — return 'No such short link exists.' WITHIN the takedown SLA, (2) behavioral — SHALL NOT redirect, and (3) instrumentation — SHALL emit a 'link_takedown_applied' event. If the instrumentation assertion (3) fails independently (e.g., the event bus is not yet wired), the test runner marks the entire scenario failed, masking whether the behavioral outcomes (1) and (2) passed. The scenario comment acknowledges this as a 'documented dual-plane verification trade-off' but does not record an explicit acceptance tag or decision reference.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) extract the 'link_takedown_applied' event assertion into a separate scenario tagged @scenario-type:success covering the observability facet of EARS.01.03.f62a, or (b) accept the co-location by adding a scenario-level tag such as '@dual-plane-accepted' with a decision reference, enabling downstream reviewers at the TDD and Code Review layers to trace the trade-off.

findings.message: The step 'Given an issued short code "/abc123" mapping to "https://example.com/page"' appears verbatim or near-verbatim in four scenarios (BDD.01.03.613b, BDD.01.03.1f90 Outline body, BDD.01.03.44fe, BDD.01.03.076f). Per C4, steps present verbatim in three or more scenarios are candidates for extraction to a shared step-definition catalog. NOTE: this project ships no step-definition catalog file; the catalog mechanism is documented as potentially framework-deferred at this single-file BDD scope.
findings.recommendation: If the step-definition catalog mechanism is confirmed as framework-deferred for this scope, record the deferral explicitly in a note at the top of §3. If not deferred, register a parameterized step definition, e.g. 'an issued short code {code} mapping to {url}', and reference it consistently. Alternatively, if these four scenarios are grouped into a sub-feature, promote the step to a Background block.

findings.message: The step 'Given destination-reputation screening is enabled' appears verbatim in three scenarios (BDD.01.03.41c7 Outline, BDD.01.03.f0a5, BDD.01.03.3708). Per C4, verbatim recurrence in three or more scenarios warrants extraction to a step-definition catalog entry. NOTE: same framework-deferral caveat applies as in QA-BDD-01-F004.
findings.recommendation: Register 'destination-reputation screening is enabled' as a named step in the step-definition catalog, or promote it to the Background block of a dedicated 'Destination Screening' sub-feature grouping these three scenarios. If deferred, document the deferral alongside QA-BDD-01-F004.

findings.message: Advisory — no upstream EARS obligation. EARS declares redirect p95 < 50 ms and >= 99.9% monthly availability as SLOs (EARS.01.04.cea3, EARS.01.04.1598) but contains no explicit breach-alert-to-channel obligation. BDD has no scenario exercising a sustained SLO breach that triggers a named paging/alerting event. Per the C5 scoping rule this is advisory only — no upstream EARS element binds the alert-fire behaviour — but the gap is real for production operability. Carried from OP-I2-ADV-003; status unchanged.
findings.recommendation: If a future EARS revision declares a breach-alert obligation (e.g., 'WHEN p95 exceeds threshold for N minutes THE system SHALL fire a named alert'), add a corresponding BDD scenario at that point. Until then this remains a known advisory gap tracked at the EARS layer.

findings.message: Advisory — no upstream EARS obligation. EARS declares destination-reputation screening as a feature gate (EARS.01.03.6811, EARS.01.03.4400) but contains no runtime-reconfig-without-restart obligation. BDD.01.03.3708 covers the gate-enabled path; there is no scenario for toggling the gate at runtime and asserting no regression. Per the C2 scoping rule this is advisory only.
findings.recommendation: If a future EARS revision declares a runtime-reconfig obligation for the screening gate (no-restart toggle), add a BDD scenario exercising gate-disable and gate-re-enable under traffic. Until then this remains a known advisory gap.
